newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SWISS SHARES END LOWER, CS, WINTERTHUR RECOVER.
newsitem.headline: SWISS SHARES END LOWER, CS, WINTERTHUR RECOVER.

text.p: 1055 GMT - Insecurity about further developments in U.S. and German interest rates led Swiss shares to a lower close.

Market attention centered on merger partners CS Group and Winterthur. Both stocks recovered from the worst of the day's losses. Winterthur added seven francs to 1,504 while CS Group ended 1.50 francs lower at 203.50.
Earlier, some analysts voiced reservations about the cost and timing of the merger, which was announced on Monday.
Many investors were seen holding back ahead of Wednesday's U.S. economic figures, dealers said.
* The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was down 1.83 points to 3,713.35.
Bourse volume was at a steep 3.61 billion Swiss francs.

CS Group and Winterthur accounted for more than a billion francs of the total turnover. Dealers said buying was led by BZ Group, the biggest Winterthur shareholder with 30 percent directly or indirectly under its control.
* Some pharmaceuticals were reportedly pressured by a downgrade by a U.S. broker. While Novartis registereds ended up four francs at 2,315, Roche ceritificates fell 165 francs to 14,140 francs.
* UBS was down four francs to 1,630.
* SBC rose two francs to 417 francs ahead of first half-year results due on Wednesday.
* Among insurers, Swiss Life jumped 100 francs ot 921, buoyed by a bigger foreign buy order.
* Insurer Zurich, which saw strong advances earlier in the session, tumbled 12 francs to 620. Dealers said selling by a smaller bank was behind the slide.
* On the Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex), SMI futures continued to be actively traded ahead of Friday's expiry of SMI August contracts.
In total, 10,176 SMI futures changed hands, of which more than 7,400 were August contracts.
On the options side, demand was high for options and warrants of CS Group and Winterthur. Total volume reached 136,677 contracts.
